explanation.en:
から means “from.” It marks the starting point of time (and sometimes place). When you say a time + から, you show when something begins.

Key points:
• Time + から = from that time
• Often pairs with まで to show a range
• The start point is included
• Used with schedules and routines

Examples: “九時から授業が始まります” means “Class starts from 9.” “三月から日本にいます” means “I will be in Japan from March.”

When you use から and まで together, you clearly show both the start and end: “九時から五時まで働きます.”

You can also use から with places, but this point focuses on time. Be sure to place から right after the time expression.

Practice by making your own schedule: 何時から勉強しますか。何時までですか。 These questions are very common in daily conversation.

examples.japanese: 九時から授業が始まります。
三月から日本にいます。
examples.english: I will be in Japan from March.

examples.japanese: 七時から九時まで勉強します。
examples.romaji: Shichi-ji kara ku-ji made benkyou shimasu.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using に instead of から for start time
commonMistakes.correction: Use から to show the beginning
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 九時に授業が始まります(meaning from) → ✅ 九時から授業が始まります

commonMistakes.correction: Add まで to show the end
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 九時から五時 → ✅ 九時から五時まで
